about: The customer panel (SPEC §0, owner 2026-10-07, issue 1304): real public sites chosen for spread, run by `npm run panel`. None is a ReachKit rival. `country` and `language` are where the business's buyers are and what its site is written in; the checks hold the pass to them. `market` is word roots of what the business is, in its own language: the concluded category has to be spoken in one of them. The order is the run order, most different kinds first, so a run its cap cuts short still covers a spread. `place` is where a business that trades in one place trades. `kinds` is the kind of business the market conclusion may record it as (SPEC §6, D69), from the closed list in `src/lib/market/kinds.ts`; a local site's `place` is also where the pass has to measure it (D67): its terms, its searches, its prompts and its rivals.

sites.why: One restaurant in San Francisco with a short site: a menu, hours and a story. Little text to read, buyers who search a cuisine and a neighbourhood, and review and booking sites all over its top tens.
A family plumbing firm in one city (Austin, Texas). Its buyers search a trade and a place, its rivals are other local plumbers, and the listings that fill its top tens (Yelp, Angi) are not rivals.
A Düsseldorf bakery whose site is in German only. Its market, terms, searches, questions and topics have to be German and measured in Germany.
An independent firm of chartered accountants in Manchester. A UK professional-services firm with many service lines and a large site: the audience and the category must stay specific.
A shop that sells one kind of product (temporary tattoos) from its own site. Its market is a product category, its rivals are other shops, and marketplaces (Amazon, Etsy) are not rivals.
A small scheduling product. The kind of site the passes were built on, in a market that is not ReachKit's: it shows whether a result is general or fitted to one site.
A design consultancy in Brighton. It sells time and expertise, not a product: its rivals are other studios, and the agency directories (Clutch) are not rivals.
One person selling web-development courses under his own name. The brand is a person, the site is mostly a blog, and course marketplaces (Udemy) are not rivals.
A dental practice in Portland, Oregon. A regulated local service with many treatments on one site: the category has to be the practice, not one treatment, and health directories must not be rivals.
A small electrical contractor in north Leeds. A trades firm outside the United States: its searches and their volumes are British, and its rivals are other Leeds electricians.
A habit-tracking app sold through the App Store, with a one-page site. Very little text, a consumer buyer, and rivals that are other apps.
